## When can community data use a diet-visualization package?

Taxonomic composition can also be described for benthic grabs, plankton
samples and other community surveys. This example follows simulated
macrofaunal grab samples with organism counts, wet mass and a local taxonomic
classification. It demonstrates DietView's hierarchy and reporting tools for
community composition. The observations are not predator diet records, and
the example makes no claim about environmental differences.

We examine how the recorded abundance and wet mass are distributed among taxa
and how much material remains identified only to a broad rank.

**Unit:** one grab of **0.1 m²** in this synthetic survey. **Quantity:**
individuals (numbers currency) and wet grams (mass currency). **Grouping:**
habitat. **Required DietView role:** `community = "Benthic grab"` is a
constant assemblage label, not a predator.

## Reproducible simulated sampling and zero samples

```{r simulate}
library(DietView)
set.seed(197)
frame <- data.frame(
  grab_id = sprintf("G%02d", 1:30),
  habitat = rep(c("sand", "mud"), each = 15),
  area_m2 = 0.1, community = "Benthic grab"
)
taxonomy <- data.frame(
  taxon = c("Hediste diversicolor", "Mytilus edulis", "Limecola balthica",
            "Gammarus sp.", "Unidentified macrofauna"),
  kingdom = rep("Animalia", 5),
  phylum = c("Annelida", "Mollusca", "Mollusca", "Arthropoda", NA),
  class = c("Polychaeta", "Bivalvia", "Bivalvia", "Malacostraca", NA),
  order = c("Phyllodocida", "Mytilida", "Cardiida", "Amphipoda", NA),
  family = c("Nereididae", "Mytilidae", "Tellinidae", "Gammaridae", NA),
  genus = c("Hediste", "Mytilus", "Limecola", "Gammarus", NA),
  species = c("Hediste diversicolor", "Mytilus edulis", "Limecola balthica",
              NA, NA)
)
i <- rep(seq_len(nrow(frame)), each = nrow(taxonomy))
j <- rep(seq_len(nrow(taxonomy)), times = nrow(frame))
n_ind <- stats::rpois(length(i), lambda = c(4, 2, 3, 6, 1.2)[j])
n_ind[i %in% c(1, 18)] <- 0L  # known grabs without recorded animals
wet_g <- round(n_ind * c(0.8, 1.4, 1.1, 0.2, 0.5)[j] *
               stats::runif(length(i), 0.8, 1.2), 3)
long <- cbind(frame[i, ], taxonomy[j, ],
              individuals = n_ind, wet_g = wet_g)
long <- long[long$individuals > 0, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(long) <- NULL
frame$empty <- !(frame$grab_id %in% long$grab_id)
head(long[, c("grab_id", "habitat", "taxon", "individuals", "wet_g")])
```

## Validate units, counts and coverage

```{r audit}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(frame$grab_id), !anyNA(long$grab_id))
stopifnot(all(long$individuals == round(long$individuals)),
          all(long$individuals >= 0), all(long$wet_g >= 0))
c(grabs_examined = nrow(frame), grabs_without_detections = sum(frame$empty),
  individuals = sum(long$individuals), wet_biomass_g = sum(long$wet_g))
```

Because all grabs have the same sampled area, their raw counts and masses are
comparably scaled in this example. If areas differ, calculate density and
biomass per area *explicitly* outside DietView before statistical comparisons;
`currency = "numbers"` is for organism counts, not fractional densities.

## Prepare the taxonomy, including unknown material

A locally checked taxonomy is supplied as **columns**. This avoids a network
lookup and makes the example reproducible. A real workflow should retain
original organism IDs, taxonomic authority/version and the rules used to
merge uncertain or outdated names.

```{r prepare}
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "community", stomach = "grab_id",
                prey_name = "taxon", count = "individuals", weight = "wet_g",
                weight_type = "mass", unit_label = "grab",
                covariates = "habitat")
prep <- dv_prepare(long, spec, taxonomy = "columns",
                   stomachs = frame, empty_col = "empty", verbose = FALSE)
prep
```

`Unidentified macrofauna` has a nonempty record with only the kingdom known;
its counts and mass remain in the denominators. **Not identified** is not
the same thing as zero organisms.

## Compare abundance and wet biomass without conflating them

```{r two-currencies}
by_records <- dv_tree(prep, currency = "records")
by_individuals <- dv_tree(prep, currency = "numbers")
rec <- dv_rank_table(by_records, "Phylum")
num <- dv_rank_table(by_individuals, "Phylum")
head(rec[, c("label", "value_occ", "pct_occ", "value_w", "pct_w")])
head(num[, c("label", "value_occ", "pct_occ", "value_w", "pct_w")])
```

In `by_individuals`, `value_occ` is the **total number of organisms** and
`pct_occ` is %N; in `by_records` they are observed taxon–grab row counts and
record shares. Both trees retain the same `value_w` (wet grams) and `pct_w`
(% of recorded wet biomass). They answer different questions and may give
different rankings.

```{r plot}
dv_sunburst(by_individuals, mode = "occurrence",
            title = "Benthic grabs: simulated individual counts",
            subtitle = "Numerical abundance, not predator diet")
```

## Occurrence frequency, taxonomic resolution and sampling

For a community survey, `dv_fo_table()` reports **grab-occurrence** (percentage
of sampled grabs where the taxon was observed). It must not be described as
predator dietary %FO. The complete grab inventory supplies the examined
sample denominator, including the two known no-detection grabs.

```{r fo}
fo <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "family", denominator = "examined")
head(fo[, c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")], 8)
```

```{r resolution}
dv_resolution(prep, by = "habitat")
dv_summary(prep, by = "habitat")
```

`dv_prey_accumulation()` can also describe the order in which *recorded taxa*
accumulate with sampled grabs. The function name retains its diet heritage,
but the sampled units here are **grabs**. Rarefaction-like curves are
*descriptive*; completeness of a habitat survey needs design-based analysis.
The function uses **grabs represented in the long table**, so known empty grabs
held only in the separate inventory do not appear on this curve's x-axis.

```{r accumulation}
acc <- dv_prey_accumulation(prep, rank = "family", permutations = 20, seed = 10)
head(acc)
```

## Export a grab × taxon matrix

```{r matrix}
m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "weight",
               include_empty = TRUE)
stopifnot(nrow(m) == nrow(frame))
c(grabs = nrow(m), taxonomic_categories = ncol(m))
head(rowSums(m))
utils::write.csv(m, file.path(tempdir(), "benthic_grab_wet_g.csv"))
```

For further analysis, examine differences in area, spatial autocorrelation,
replicate grabs, mesh size, wet-weight measurement error and zero inflation.
The exported values are raw **grams per grab**, not a calibrated biomass
surface for the habitat.

```{r optional-dashboard, eval=FALSE}
dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "benthic_grabs_demo.html"),
  strata = "habitat", currency = "numbers",
  bands = c("occurrence", "weight"),
  title = "Benthic community composition (simulated; not a diet)")
```

## Reporting summary

Include sample-frame coverage, gear and grab area, taxonomic version, units,
preprocessing, empty vs failed samples, number of individuals, mass
measurement, unidentified share, replication and uncertainty. Do **not** turn
a nice sunburst into a claim about predator feeding, ecosystem change or
habitat preference: those conclusions require additional data and inference.
For the equivalent *catch composition* workflow, see
[the survey catch case](case-study-survey-catch.html).
